charts.title: A slow STT vendor no longer makes the agent deaf
charts.subtitle: Longest single process_inbound_pcm call (one 20 ms audio frame) while the STT vendor is slow. Same tests on each release. Lower is better. Log scale.
rows: STT final 3.3 s late, Finalized 3 s late
STT final 10 s late, next phrase 1 s later
charts.note: VoiceAgent + cluster speech client + mock speech server over gRPC, inbound frame every 20 ms. The 0.11.2 tests were copied into the 0.9.48 and 0.10.0 checkouts with compile fixes only (perf-data/2026-10-16/slow-stt). Since 0.11.0 each agent runs STT in its own task.

charts.title: DTLS handshakes that never finish on a lossy link
charts.subtitle: Handshakes stuck out of 200 concurrent ones, by packet loss. The server never resent its last flight, so one lost datagram left the client hanging. Lower is better.
charts.note: Seeded lossy-pipe stress test. The patched build also stays at 0 / 200 at 50 % loss and with reordering and delay. RFC 6347 §4.2.4 fix proposed upstream as webrtc-rs/webrtc#921.

charts.title: Two-thirds less work on the Node.js main thread
charts.subtitle: JS main-thread CPU of a voice host serving 10 concurrent sessions (STT, TTS, language ID, client mix). Median of 3 runs. Lower is better.
charts.axisLabel: ms of JS main-thread CPU per second
charts.note: start:roundtrip-counting-echo-lid-multi, echo-server process, scripts/perf/js-thread-probe.mjs. Whole-process CPU fell from 697 to 580–586 ms/s. Apple M4 Pro, 2026-10-16, versions alternated per run.

charts.title: Runs where every turn was heard correctly
charts.subtitle: Same machine, same day, versions alternated. A run fails on any lost, doubled or wrong word. Higher is better.
rows: Capacity ramp up to its latency limit (2 runs)
10 sessions with ~10 % of a CPU (3 runs)
charts.note: 0.9.48 failures: 7 sessions with a doubled "nine", 1 of 40 turns misheard, a misheard turn at 20 legs, a lost "Okay" under starvation. 0.10.0: a misheard turn at 20 legs. Starvation = SIGSTOP duty cycle 5 ms run / 45 ms stop.

charts.title: Concurrent voice loopbacks in one process
charts.subtitle: Final-transcript latency p95 per load step. A step passes while p95 stays within 1 s of the 2-leg step. Lower and further right is better.
charts.xLabel: concurrent speaker/listener legs (Sherpa TTS → WebRTC → Sherpa STT)
charts.note: start:roundtrip-load capacity mode, 2 turns per leg, Apple M4 Pro, 2026-10-16. The longer of two rounds per version is shown. In the other round 0.9.48 and 0.10.0 stopped at the 20-leg step on one misheard turn, and 0.11.2 again reached 40 legs. Final latency sits near 2 s because of the VAD end-of-turn wait.
